about: AI-written, 11 November 2026. Five AI readers reviewed the branch before it landed, one angle each (the tool, the truth of the page, the reader, the integration, the record); they read and ran no tests. Their reports are kept as they came, but for the address of one private page, cut where a report quotes it. README.md says what was changed on them and what was left for the director.

findings.title: Each card's misfit note is cut at 320 characters without a mark, and the cut can turn a sentence around
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:242 (join: 'misfit': c['misfit'][:320]); shown in tools/research/the_map.html:216
findings.what: join() keeps only the first 320 characters of every card's misfit, and the map to operate shows that under "What the map's kinds do not hold here" with no ellipsis and no link to the rest. THE-MAP.md says "The note is on the map to operate, under each dynamic." 178 of 183 cards are longer than 320 characters (many run 600 to 2,400), so almost every note stops mid-clause. At least one stops at a point that reverses its meaning.
findings.evidence: In cards.json, reading-a-loss-in-time's misfit reads "...best-open's further claim (that the actual system is at the best) is not needed; but...". interactive.html carries it as "...(that the actual system is at the best) is " (grep confirms the string ends there). 178/183 truncated notes do not end in '.' or ')'. The full notes would add 93,385 bytes; interactive.html is 1,711,835 bytes, so the total stays under MAX_INTERACTIVE (1,950,000).
findings.fix: Drop the [:320] slice and pass the whole misfit (it fits). If size ever needs a cut, cut at a sentence end and add '…' plus 'the rest in the card'.

findings.title: A law filed under another dynamic is shown with no conditions, though its card names them
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:223-224 (took = takes.get((d, l['lean']))...; main = [...] or took[:3])
findings.what: A law's conditions are looked up only by (this dynamic, law). When the law is a declaration of this dynamic but the ledger files its premises under a different dynamic, `took` is empty. Then main=[] and more=0, the card's own main_ifs are thrown away, and the map to operate shows the law with no "if", so it looks unconditional. The same law shows its conditions on one card and none on another. validate() does not report the dropped main_ifs.
findings.evidence: 16 laws whose card names main_ifs (all ids present in premises.json) come out with main=[]; 15 of them are filed under another dynamic. Example: Becoming.Web.consumed_continues_transformed has main [] on loss-of-renewal-for-good and ['k3-activity-needing-support','web-below-need-after','web-active'] on three-outcomes-of-a-loss. Across all cards, 51 main_ifs entries are silently dropped.
findings.fix: When (d, law) is not in takes, fall back to the takes of any dynamic in filed[law], or keep the card's main_ifs that exist in the ledger. Have validate() report a main_ifs id that is in neither.

findings.title: The 'mixed' square says the opposite of what the one mixed test records
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:575 (said['mixed']); tools/research/the_map.html:269
findings.what: The page labels the mixed square "It differs by system: One system met it and another did not." Its only test met the "if" in both systems; what differed was whether the "then" was seen. The map to operate goes further wrong: it puts mixed tests in the "The 'if' was not checked: Nothing can be read off yet" box.
findings.evidence: squares['mixed'] = ['IN1 (round 2)'] with square_said 'if met, then seen (gpt-5.4-mini); if met, then not seen (gpt-4.1-mini)'. THE-MAP.md line 514: '| It differs by system (1) | [IN1 (round 2)](...) | One system met it and another did not. |'. Template line 269 counts D.squares['if not checked'].length + D.squares.mixed.length under 'The "if" was not checked'.
findings.fix: Word the mixed square neutrally, e.g. 'It differs by system: see the case' and show square_said beside each test. Give mixed its own box in the template instead of merging it into 'if not checked'.

findings.title: The ledger plainer cuts mid-word and leaves broken fragments of formulas
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:191-197 (plain)
findings.what: The parenthesis-dropping regex cannot match nested parentheses. A nested formula is either kept whole or has only its inner group removed, which leaves a garbled formula behind. The [:200] cut falls mid-word with no ellipsis.
findings.evidence: Sample of 30 premises used. 'regimemargin-drawn-not-down' comes out as '...in both level and recent giving (¬ D.Below p)', and the original was '(¬ D.Below (D.step A H p) p)'. 'livingorganizationcorrespondence-all-closed' keeps '(∀ r, allowed r → Closed pool (recipes r))'. 'representation-balanced-paths' ends '...amounts read in' and 'closedcapture-drawn-pool' ends '...each counted '. Of the 939 used premises, 36 are cut at 200 and 57 still hold ∀/∃/≤/→/↔/∧, a dotted name or :=.
findings.fix: Remove balanced parenthesised groups by iterating the regex until nothing changes, or by depth scan. Apply the formula test to the whole statement and keep the head before ': ' when the tail is formal. Cut at a word boundary and add '…'.

findings.title: Count wording: '773 of 2073' and 'in the atlas / not' do not mean what they say
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:303-310 (counts laws, laws_named_*); THE-MAP.md 'What the map shows today'; tools/research/the_map.html:138,144
findings.what: counts['laws'] counts card law items, not distinct Lean laws, and some are not among the atlas laws with premises that all_laws counts. So 'X of Y' reads as a subset when it is not one. The template's 'Laws a prediction names: ... {{laws_named_atlas}} are in the atlas, {{laws_named_off}} are not' calls 75 laws 'not in the atlas', but 6 of them are atlas declarations. The page's own wording, 'among the atlas's laws with premises', is right. The template's line 138 also drops 'with premises'.
findings.evidence: 773 law entries, 726 distinct Lean names, 719 of those distinct in the 2073; 45 Lean names appear on more than one card. named=145, off premises=75, and 6 of those 75 are declared in the atlas (e.g. Becoming.DrawnShaping.favours_everywhere_iff, Becoming.RegimeMargin.step).
findings.fix: Report distinct laws as 'N write-ups of M distinct Lean laws', and count the subset against all_laws as len(distinct & atlas_laws). In the template, use the page's wording 'among the atlas's laws with premises' on lines 138 and 144.

findings.title: A tie whose only law for a mark is 'outside' is counted as having none, yet the page quotes a law for it
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:276 (marks exclude outside) vs 489/552-553 (_best returns an outside law when it is the only one)
findings.what: The ties table and 'Drawn ties where no principal law shows an end: 13' count a tie as having no law for a mark when its only law for that mark holds only if a given were otherwise. Under the same tie, the bullet for that mark quotes the law. The square in the picture stays empty. The table's preamble does explain the rule, but the summary row ('no principal law shows') contradicts the bullet a reader finds under the tie.
findings.evidence: gives-back|renewer|stock: table 'Ends' 0, while THE-MAP.md line 103 shows '- **Ends.** After the first step the rate of giving back is below its initial value ... Only if something taken as given were otherwise.' Same for reaches|stock|rule 'Lasts' (line 164).
findings.fix: Word the summary row as 'no general law of the course itself shows', or label such a bullet '(no general law; one if a given were otherwise)'.

findings.title: validate() lets through data that makes join(), page() or the page's script crash
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:101-188
findings.what: Several fields are read without being checked, and a missing one raises out of render() as an exception that stops research.py instead of coming back as an error. These are: role/tie en, zh, is and account (page:525,549; drawing:402,411), prediction from_laws (join:253), prediction ifs (join:298 reads p['ifs'] directly, though validate uses p.get('ifs') or []), built_cases lean and shows_en (join:242), and an empty strength string (validate:155, ''.split()[0] raises IndexError). In the script, a thing with no thing_en throws in paint() (html:250: xs[0].thing_en.split). A non-legend card with no ties passes unnoticed. In main(), --fragment calls geometry() outside the try that render() has.
findings.evidence: Checked against the real data: every role and tie has en/zh/is/account; no prediction lacks from_laws or ifs; every thing has thing_en; every built case has lean and shows_en; no card has an about of bool type. Today, two placed (non-legend) cards have no ties: what-a-gate-keeps and seeking-boundary. They show an empty Ties cell and light no tie.
findings.fix: Add these required keys to validate() (roles en/zh/is/account; ties en/zh/is; predictions from_laws/ifs/label/says_en; things thing_en; built_cases lean/shows_en; strength non-empty). Flag a card with legend false and no ties, or treat it as legend.

findings.title: fill() substitutes {{key}} over the inlined data and drawing
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:623-627
findings.what: The {{count}} replacements run after /*DATA*/ and /*MAP*/ are inserted. Any card or case text containing '{{tests}}', '{{laws}}' or the like would be silently changed in the data and the drawing.
findings.evidence: The real data has no '{{' and no '/*' (checked over json.dumps(model)), so nothing is affected today.
findings.fix: Do the {{key}} replacements on the template first, then insert MAP and DATA last.

findings.title: The map to operate shows the raw word 'witness'; the page says 'one built case'
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.html:157,169
findings.what: HOW has no 'witness' entry, so 28 witness laws show the bare internal word, while the page's _said() writes 'one built case'.
findings.evidence: Strengths in the model: sufficient 537, exact 176, necessary 32, witness 28. html:157 HOW = {exact, sufficient, necessary} only.
findings.fix: Add witness: 'one built case' to HOW.

findings.title: Tests promise things they do not check: determinism, the size guard, field presence
findings.where: tools/research/tests/test_the_map.py
findings.what: No test renders twice, or under another hash seed, and compares bytes. No test drives render() over MAX_INTERACTIVE to see the guard's error. No test covers a missing role/tie field or a missing prediction field. No test checks that a misfit note or a law's conditions survive the join (the two high findings above would have been caught). test_the_counts_agree_with_one_another's last assertion (placed == counts['laws']) holds by construction of join(). The other assertions there are real.
findings.evidence: I ran the_map.render() in process under PYTHONHASHSEED 1, 2 and 977. The three outputs were byte-identical each time and equal to the files in the worktree, which also equal /Users/ren/tmp/rw/site/mapcheck/. So determinism holds today, but no test checks it.
findings.fix: Add a test that renders twice and compares bytes; a test that monkeypatches MAX_INTERACTIVE small and expects the error; a JoinTests case for a law filed under another dynamic; a check that the model's misfit equals the card's.

findings.title: In the static views, a met thin tie gives no dot or ring to the drawn tie it is listed under
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:283-292, 399-400, 448-451
findings.what: reach and near are computed per edge, and the dot or ring is drawn from the drawn edge's own values. A thinner tie's tests are not carried up to the head it is shown_as, while the script's paint() does map met and near edges to shown_as. The SVG and the interactive view can therefore disagree.
findings.evidence: gives-to|stock|stock (thin) has near 3; its head gives-to|pattern|pattern has reach 0 and near 0, so it gets no ring in the-map.svg. When a test bearing on it is chosen in the map to operate, paint() lights the head.
findings.fix: Either fold a thin edge's reach/near into its head for the drawing, or say in the key that marks count only the drawn tie itself.

reports.checked:
I read the whole of tools/research/the_map.py, the_map.html and tests/test_the_map.py, plus the research.py diff and registry.finish. I ran short read-only Python against the worktree's data:
- load, validate (returns no errors) and join.
- Field presence for every place the code reads a field.
- Lengths of the misfit notes, and what the truncation does.
- Real-data scans for |, <, *, _, [ ], backticks, newlines, {{, /*, <!--, <script, U+2028/2029 and « » in law sentences, plain sentences, names, web strings and Lean names.
- plain() on a seeded sample of 30 of the 939 premises used.
- Each count's meaning against the atlas.
- Laws whose mark comes only from an outside law, and how thin ties' tests reach their drawn heads.
- Squares and the mixed test.
- Dropped main_ifs.
- Person words in the other sentence fields.
- the_map.render() in process (it writes nothing) under three PYTHONHASHSEED values.

I ran no test suite, no research.py render, gate, make, Lean or site build.
reports.notes:
The outputs are deterministic. Under three hash seeds, render() gave byte-identical output equal to the files in the worktree, and the worktree files equal the mapcheck copies. Every set that reaches the output is sorted first: also, dynamics, edges/near, tests, prem, fails, thin. Insertion order everywhere else comes from the JSON files.

Escaping is safe on today's data:
- html.escape guards the SVG text and attributes. The data-role and data-edge ids, and the family/id in the script's atlas href, are not escaped, but they are atlas ids.
- The JSON in <script> has '</' turned into '<\/'. The data holds no '<!--', no '<script' and no U+2028/2029.
- In Markdown, the only hazards found are 'γ<β' (no tag can start there), '[P, Q]' (literal) and 'K_N' (inside a word). « » appear only inside backticks.
- The roles-table cells r['en']/r['zh'] and the thin-tie list items do not go through _cell, but none holds a hazard today.

Two choices are defensible but could be said more exactly. _best() sorts general before outside, then exact < sufficient < necessary < witness, then card order; the page's 'the strongest first' is only roughly right, since it ranks necessary below sufficient. SCORED counts 'could not tell' as scored: 4 such predictions name laws, which feeds the green dot's 'a scored prediction names a law here'.

The word rule finds no hit in misfit, built shows_en, cast/ties 'as' or the web fields. 'agents' (a-code-held-as-counts) and 'members'/'taught' (a-rule-with-no-holder-does-not-return) appear in law sentences. They are the models' own terms and not clearly person-only, so I did not count them as defects. The two '们' in then_zh are '它们'.

The JS has no throwing path on real data:
- A tie with no laws falls back to its message.
- A role with no ties renders an empty list.
- The two tests with no predictions (circular-construction, valuation-development) render.
- No case names the role 'any'.

The generated files are mode 600, which git ignores apart from the exec bit.

findings.title: "Lean modules" counts namespace prefixes, not modules
findings.where: tools/research/the_map.py:285 (e['modules']); THE-MAP.md ties table column "Lean modules", every tie heading ("proved in N separate Lean modules"), and the bullet "A tie gathers separate models" (line 538)
findings.what: The count is len({'.'.join(lean.split('.')[:2])}). That gives the first namespace segment, not a Lean module or file. Top-level theorems each count as their own "module", and one namespace spread over many files counts once. The page then offers this number as the evidence of how many separate models a tie gathers.
findings.evidence: On a stock · reaches · a stock (9 "modules"), the prefixes include 'Becoming.gap_polynomial_iff_no_loop', 'Becoming.onLoop_succ_iff', 'Becoming.break_carried_nowhere' and 'Becoming.carried_le_polynomial_before': each theorem name is its own "module". Their files are Loops.lean, Closing.lean, Thresholds.lean and Closing.lean, so carried_le_polynomial_before and onLoop_succ_iff share Closing.lean but count as two. On draws-on, Web.consumingIn_kept_iff and Substitution.consuming_through_sustaining both sit in Substitution.lean and count as two modules. 'Becoming.Web' counts once although `namespace Web` opens in 64 files. 63 distinct card laws have no namespace (Becoming.x).
findings.fix: Count source files: resolve each declaration to its .lean file, for example from the atlas or the Lean catalogue. Or rename the column "namespaces" and drop the sentence that uses it as evidence of separate models.

findings.title: One square per test hides mixed results; "They agree" lists tests whose records are mixed
findings.where: THE-MAP.md "Where reasoning has met a case" table (lines 509-515); cases.json 'square'; the_map.py page() said{}
findings.what: Each test gets one hand-chosen square, but its predictions spread over several. The row "The 'if' was met, and the 'then' was seen (11) ... They agree" includes tests whose own records are mixed or gave no verdict. Some other placements also contradict the case's own data. The page never says the square summarises only part of a test.
findings.evidence: tests.json outcome for tests in the "They agree" row: CG2 mixed ("nine passed and two failed"; 2 of 6 predictions disagreed, failed_at bridge, each with an if failed), MQ2 mixed ("4 of 8 passed"), MQ1 (simulation) mixed, VD2 mixed (3 of 6 disagreed), TR2A no-verdict. CG1 is placed in "if not met, then not seen", yet its A1 and A2 agreed with every if met. LA1 is placed in "if met, then not seen ... A bridge, a measure, a scoring rule or a thesis gave way", yet all 3 misses are failed_at power and its resolution "if" is 'not checked'. FC1 is placed in "if not met, then seen ... something no law here covers", yet none of its 4 predictions names a law or a thesis (from_laws [] and from_thesis '' throughout); its ifs are coding-procedure conditions. MQ3 (all failed_at if) and LA2 fit their squares.
findings.fix: Place squares per prediction, or show each test's spread (for example "CG2: 4 met-seen, 2 met-not-seen"). At least say that a test's square is the case's summary and give its record's outcome beside it. Move FC1 to the "no prediction of the account" row, and LA1 to "if not checked" or a power row.

findings.title: Squares filled by a single built case (witness) are said to "show what makes it so"
findings.where: THE-MAP.md lines 13 and 539-540, the-map.svg <desc>, the_map.html line 102; the_map.py summary() line 276
findings.what: marks[m] counts every non-outside tie law, witnesses included. Two drawn squares are filled only by a witness, which shows that the mark can occur in one model, not what makes it so. The counts in "Drawn ties where no principal law shows" are low by one each for beginnings and changes on that reading.
findings.evidence: passes-on Begins is filled by 2 laws, both witness (Recycle.closed_unceasing, printed "one built case"). set-from Changes is filled by 1 witness (RuleCapture.Alternating.alternates, "In one built case..."). So of the 2 drawn ties with a Changes square filled, one rests on a built case only. Without witnesses the counts would be beginnings 14, changes 18.
findings.fix: Exclude strength 'witness' from marks, or draw witness-only squares differently (for example half-filled), and say so in the legend and the desc.

findings.title: "A law that holds only if something taken as given were otherwise is not counted there" is false for Borders, Unmoved by and Cannot
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 38; the_map.py summary() line 277 ('forms' counts every non-tie law)
findings.what: Only the four marks leave out by_outside laws. The Borders, Unmoved by and Cannot columns count them, although the page's lead treats these as questions too. Separately, the page prints an outside law under a question its count and square say has none.
findings.evidence: Outside laws counted in drawn ties' form columns: selects border 7, alike 1, cannot 1; draws-on cannot 1; passes-on cannot 2; needs border 1; stock-stock border 1; subject-readers alike 1. That makes 15 (my recount). gives-back shows Ends 0 in the table, and the page says no drawn tie... yet line 103 prints an Ends law ("Only if..."). The same holds for reaches stock→rule Lasts (line 164).
findings.fix: Apply `not l['outside']` in the forms Counter too, or limit the sentence to Begins to Ends. Either show outside laws under a separate label or say that a quoted law does not fill the square.

findings.title: The lead says every law is about one tie; 337 of 773 principal laws are about a single role or none and never appear on the page
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 9 ("A law of the account says something general about one tie"), the_map.html line 91
findings.what: Laws with about_role (a role, or 'any') are joined to role_laws and never reach the page's tables or tie sections. The ties table's "Principal laws" column covers only the tie laws.
findings.evidence: My count of cards.json laws: edge 436; role:stock 122, any 106, pattern 49, dependent 19, selected 15, reading 13, drawers 4, parts 3, rule 3, readers 2, renewer 1, which makes 337. The page states "Principal laws written up: 773".
findings.fix: Say "a law says something general about one tie or one role" and give the split (436 on ties, 337 on a role or on every course). Optionally add a short per-role section.

findings.title: perfect_at_floors sentence drops its key premise and over-quantifies
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 88 (draws-on, Lasts); cards.json law Becoming.Optimum.InTurn.perfect_at_floors
findings.what: The sentence says "In every perfect profile every drawer leaves exactly its floor". The Lean statement holds only where two drawers have no floor. Placing it under "Lasts" is also doubtful: it says where drawing stands, not that something lasts.
findings.evidence: Optimum.lean:8363: `theorem perfect_at_floors {u v : Nat} (uv : u < v) (vk : v < k) (freeU : ∀ t a, low u t a = 0) (freeV : ∀ t a, low v t a = 0) (perfect : Perfect G low rules k N) ... : ∀ d, d < k → ∀ a, rules d t a = low d t a`. The docstring reads "Where two drawers have no floor, every perfect profile is the floor profile".
findings.fix: then_en: "Where two drawers have no floor, in every perfect profile every drawer leaves exactly its floor at every step before the horizon, from every level." Reconsider the mark.

findings.title: Person-word check is a short regex; worker/reviewer/roster/hearer pass, yet the page says such a word stops the render
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 546; the_map.py PERSON_EN (lines 62-63); cards.json joint-practice-forms-continuation and a-code-formed-between-formations
findings.what: The page says a card whose sentence "uses a word that fits only a person" stops the render. The check only catches the listed words. Law sentences printed on the page and in the interactive use worker, reviewer, roster and hearer. These are the Lean model's own terms, which the roles section allows, so whether they break the director's rule is uncertain. Still, the claim about what the render enforces is broader than the code.
findings.evidence: Line 178: "The round completes exactly where worker and reviewer are present, distinct, the reviewer on the roster ..." (MachineInstances.round_iff; the Lean names them `r` reviewer and `w` worker, `s.org.roster`). Line 138: "the hearer's code". My scan of then_en also found 'agents' x2 and 'decides' x1.
findings.fix: Say "uses a word on the map's list of person-words". Then decide whether model terms like worker and reviewer should be re-said in role-words (for example "the one revised" and "the one reading").

findings.title: "773 of 2073" compares law entries with distinct Lean names
findings.where: THE-MAP.md lines 525 and 539; the_map.py counts 'laws' versus 'all_laws'
findings.what: 773 counts card law entries, so a law filed on two cards counts twice. 2073 counts distinct Lean names in the atlas premises, and some card laws are not among them at all.
findings.evidence: My recount: 773 entries, 726 distinct Lean names, of which 719 are among the 2073; 7 are not, only declarations. The atlas's premise rows number 2181.
findings.fix: Report "726 distinct Lean laws (773 entries on cards), 719 of the 2073 the atlas lists with premises".

findings.title: The interactive map truncates every card's "what the kinds do not hold" note to 320 characters
findings.where: the_map.py join() line 242 (c['misfit'][:320]); THE-MAP.md line 537 ("The note is on the map to operate, under each dynamic")
findings.what: 181 of the 183 notes are longer than 320 characters (median 797, longest 2377). The interactive shows them cut mid-sentence with no mark.
findings.evidence: `'misfit': c['misfit'][:320]`; the_map.html line 216 shows d.misfit as is.
findings.fix: Drop the slice, since the size budget allows it, or cut at a sentence end and add an ellipsis with a link to cards.json.

findings.title: "A card takes ... the laws its exits and transitions cite" overstated
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 539
findings.what: Many cited laws are neither a card law nor a built case.
findings.evidence: Of the laws cited by atlas exits and transitions, 18 exit laws and 39 transition declarations in 24 cards are on neither. Examples: margin-of-a-regime lacks Becoming.RegimeMargin.not_before; consumption-ends-with-feeders lacks Becoming.Overshoot.steady_continues; a-rule-with-no-holder-does-not-return lacks RuleRebuilding.«恒取不逾生则存».
findings.fix: Say "most of the laws its exits and transitions cite", or add the missing ones.

findings.title: "None is placed on a proved law" is true by the schema, and the failure tally mixes outcomes
findings.where: THE-MAP.md line 517; the_map.py FAILED_AT
findings.what: FAILED_AT has no value for a law, so the sentence cannot come out otherwise; it reads as a finding. The tally is introduced as places of "a disagreement or a failure". It also counts failed_at on agreed predictions, while two disagreements have no place.
findings.evidence: FAILED_AT = ('none','bridge','if','law-to-prediction','measure','scoring rule','records','power'). failed_at set on agreed predictions: 6 (bridge 2, scoring rule 2, if 1, measure 1). Disagreed with failed_at none: TR2A, UE32. The page's list "a bridge, a measure, a scoring rule or a thesis" also leaves out the record's own categories law-to-prediction (6), power (13) and records (8).
findings.fix: Say "the cases have no place for a failure of a proved law: a case can fail at ..." and list all the categories. Count only disagreed or could-not-tell predictions, or say the count is over all predictions.

findings.title: The "Scored tests" column is not what the page's other sentences suggest
findings.where: THE-MAP.md ties table, last column; the_map.py line 284 (e['near'])
findings.what: The column counts scored tests that bear on any dynamic speaking of the tie, through c['dynamics'] or a named law filed under that dynamic. It does not count tests whose predictions name a law on this tie. With no explanation, "29" on draws-on sits beside the summary row saying that a scored prediction names a principal law on only 4 drawn ties.
findings.evidence: draws-on 29, gives-back 25, needs 24 scored tests. Drawn ties where a scored prediction names a law on the tie: 4 (my recount: draws-on, needs, selects, reaches stock→rule).
findings.fix: Rename the column "Scored tests bearing on its dynamics", or add a column of tests whose predictions name a law here.

findings.title: A few law sentences are filed under a doubtful question
findings.where: THE-MAP.md lines 212, 142, 164
findings.what: These filings are doubtful readings of the statement; none of the sentences is false. certified_available_iff is filed under Lasts but concludes giving at step 1 only. Diagonal.complete_iff_alike is filed under Border, though web.json defines border as "exactly where one amount or time is at least another" and the statement compares no amount or time (all values equal). observed_raise_couples is filed under Lasts, though it concludes that a raise reaches through the couplings.
findings.evidence: Tolerance.lean:546 `... (Law.run (certified roster faults) ...).state 1 a = true) ↔ separated ...`. Diagonal.lean:133 `(∃ ψ, ∀ g, Says Eq ψ g) ↔ ∀ b b' : B, b = b'`. Runaway.lean:162 `¬ W.AlikeThrough obs g W.level (W.raise c d).level t`.
findings.fix: Re-file them: certified_available_iff as a border or a begins (giving restored at step 1), complete_iff_alike as cannot or same-as, and observed_raise_couples as reaches, not lasts. Or widen the border form's definition.

findings.title: Doubtful Chinese names and sentences (for the director's revision)
findings.where: web.json roles/ties zh; cards.json then_zh
findings.what: Role and tie names. 读法 (a reading): means 'way of reading / pronunciation', not a view or a prediction held; 读数, 所见 or 解读 would fit better (52 uses). 所选者 (what it selects among): means 'what is selected', not the candidates; 候选者 or 待选者 would fit. 延续者: 者 makes a 'continuer' sound like an agent; 所续 or 延续之物 would avoid that. 补给者: 补给 is military or logistics supply; 回补者 would fit. 读取者: 读取 is computer-ish, and the account says 读者; the sentences use both, 37 vs 11, sometimes in one dynamic (ReaderRebuilding). 相与 (gives to, waiting on): classical 'to get along'; it loses the waiting, and 相待而与 or 待与 would keep it. 选 alone loses 'favours'; 选而偏向 would keep it. 由…定出 and 经…而读 read as calques. Marks: 生住异亡 departs from the usual 生住异灭; if intended, say so. Carriers appear as both 承载者 (29) and 携带者 (22). 'Formation' as a count noun 每个形成/个形成 (39 uses) is unnatural Chinese. Sampled sentences that read wrong or translated: (a) Flow.widens_iff_within_margin_at '有这部分的水平宽于没有它的…' says 'the level is wider', but the English is 'widens what can form'. That is a mistranslation. (b) Optimum frontier laws '这一所需在第一步即亡' / '所需住到第 n 步，在末步亡': the need does not die; its being met ends, so 所需在第一步即不得满足 / 依存于末步断. (c) Withholding.withholding_absorbs '给自第 d 步起亡' would read better as 自第 d 步起再无给予. (d) Undecided.liar_rests_iff '其值住过一步' would read better as 其值到下一步不变. (e) SharedCodes.run_kept_iff '相合住到下一步' (住到 is used 9 times as a calque of 'lasts to'). (f) Law.rise_not_lossless '表明这条规律并非不合并；哪两个状态被并，并未指出' would read better as 表明此律必把某两个状态合一，只是未指出哪两个. (g) Reproduction.Mutation.balanced_iff '第一步平衡（选择一项对传递所减）' is garbled; 选择项与传递所减相抵 would fix it. (h) re-optimizing laws '所需得及', '此后永不复及': 及 here means 'met' but is also the name of the 'reaches' tie; 得到满足 / 不再满足 would avoid the clash. (i) 亡 is used of stocks, couplings and giving (存量亡, 耦合亡而不复, 给…亡). For non-living things 尽, 断 or 止 reads more naturally, though 亡 may be the deliberate mark word.
findings.evidence: Counts in then_zh and plain_zh: 读法 52, 读取者 37 vs 读者 11, 承载者 29 vs 携带者 22, 个形成 39, 住到 9, 偏好 12 vs 偏向 30. Sentences quoted above from a seeded sample of 25.

reports.notes: Judging words: web.json's role, tie, mark and form names are almost free of judgment. 'favours', 'accords or misses', 'reaches or lies beyond', begins/lasts/changes/ends and 'cannot' all describe what happens. The one value-tinged name is the frame 'the best of what is open'; 'the top of an order among what is open' would be neutral. The page's own prose uses 'wrong' only in 'cannot make a proved law wrong' and 'what a test can show wrong' (lines 9, 505), and 'failure' or 'gave way' for bridges and measures (lines 510, 517). These describe test outcomes, not values. Judging words on the page come from atlas titles and card plain sentences: 'A wrong projection', 'a wrong ranking', 'safe in every world' (line 340), 'faithful copy' (line 428), 'the right method' (line 385), 'a reward for keeping below that total fails, one above works' (line 461), 'false confidence' (line 377), 'Degeneration', 'Obscuration', 'Position does not protect'.
